_about: What stands open (M7; design/case/prior-art-investigation-ux.md §1, item 1): the Justice's open questions for case-1660, shown in the notebook's first tab. Each is raised and closed by the narrator's condition language (src/make/narrator.js; also said:WHO/any, once that person has been questioned at all); no raised means open from the arrival. where names whom to ask or where to go, never the answer; who lists the people it names, whose present room the notebook adds. side: a herring's question the shortest solution need not settle (still closable in one question). Evaluated by src/make/leads.js; checked by node tests/.leads.mjs (every expression parses and names real things; along the _fairness solution path every lead raised is closed, a side one closable in one more question). To be merged into case-1660.json as its leads.

leads.text: Who is in the house this morning, and where shall I find them?
leads.closed: said:household or (said:daniel/any and said:cressy/any and said:francis/any)
leads.where: Dame Anne will tell you who is in the house.

leads.text: What is to be seen in the room where he lay?
leads.where: The muniment room: up the great stair, through the best bedchamber and the closet beyond it.

leads.text: Did he fall against the chest in the dark, as Sir Gervase will have it, or was he struck?
leads.where: Ask how he died of whoever laid him out; look at the chest's corner.

leads.text: Struck from behind, with something round: with what?
leads.where: The muniment room: whatever stood within reach of him last night.

leads.text: Who had a key to the muniment room?
leads.where: Ask Dame Anne, or the clerk who keeps the muniment door, of the door and its keys.

leads.text: His key-cord was cut at his girdle. Where is the key now?
leads.where: The muniment room, where the door was locked upon him.

leads.text: Was the key truly by his hand when the door was opened this morning?
leads.raised: learned:daniel_says_key_by_hand or learned:key_cut_cord or learned:anne_girdle_cord or learned:body_cord
leads.where: Those who stood at the door at dawn: the clerk went in first; Dame Anne held the light.

leads.text: Who was with Mr Hollins among his deeds last night, and until what hour?
leads.closed: learned:daniel_says_half_ten or learned:daniel_went_up or learned:anne_visit or learned:daniel_lady_left
leads.where: His clerk, Daniel Wragg, who keeps the muniment door.

leads.text: Who saw the clerk come down the great stair at half past ten?
leads.where: Whoever sat up last night where the stair foot can be seen: the great parlour's door gives on it.

leads.text: If not at half past ten, when did the clerk come down, and who saw him?
leads.where: Those who were up past eleven: Master Francis and Mr Cressy, at tables in the great parlour.

leads.text: Whose blood was on Master Francis's hand and shirt at one in the morning?
leads.where: Master Francis, of his cut hand; or Mr Cressy, who sat at tables with him.

leads.text: Was Mr Cressy on the great stair at half past ten, as the clerk says?
leads.where: Whoever sat at tables with Mr Cressy last night.

leads.text: Why did Dame Anne go up to the muniment room at ten at night, and when did she come down?
leads.where: Dame Anne herself, pressed on where she was; or anyone who was in that room, or could see the stair.

leads.text: What did Mr Hollins find when he read the engrossment against his draft?
leads.raised: learned:daniel_says_half_ten or learned:daniel_went_up or learned:daniel_engrossed or learned:cressy_took_deed or learned:anne_cressy_pale or learned:anne_visit or learned:drawer_asshover
leads.closed: learned:rasure or learned:draft_exception or learned:cressy_cheat or learned:cressy_bribe
leads.where: The engrossment, on the draw-table in the great chamber where Mr Cressy keeps it; and the draft, wherever it has gone.

leads.text: Twenty pieces of gold in a clerk's box, and a note signed A.C.: who paid him, and for what?
leads.where: Mr Cressy, whose initials those may be.

leads.text: Why has the clerk run up to the garret, white as whey?
leads.closed: done:cornered or opened:box_daniel or holding:draft_steward or learned:gold_note or learned:draft_exception
leads.where: The servants' chamber in the west garret, up the back stair beyond the kitchen.

leads.text: Have I enough to lay before the coroner: who, why, by what means, when, and how the door was locked?
leads.where: The household waits in the great hall. Accuse, from any conversation.
